description: The MOM5 ocean general circulation model, developed based on the Geophysical Fluid Dynamics Laboratory, is designed to simulate global large-scale wind-driven circulation and thermohaline circulation. MOM5 uses a quasi‑Eulerian framework with a generalized z‑coordinate, and a tripolar grid with Arakawa B‑grid staggering .  It is based on the hydrostatic primitive equations and the Boussinesq approximation, including a comprehensive set of physical processes with advanced parameterization schemes. This model serves as the oceanic component of the BCC-CSM3 coupled climate model, with a uniform global horizontal resolution of 1/4° and 50 layers in the vertical. It has a rotated bipolar grid north of 65°N that situates two poles on land (at 65°N, 100°W and 65°N, 80°E) to remove the northern ocean singularity, while the remaining pole is placed at the South Pole.
references: S. M.: Elements of the Modular Ocean Model (MOM)
